courses.title: Singing for the Actor II
courses.description: Continuing vocal technique for the musical theatre. More complicated musical material investigated and prepared.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Production Practicum
courses.description: Taken each term by all graduate contemporary dance making and performance students. The class supports candidates in their ongoing research in the development of performance work for all three years from in-studio showings through thesis presentation. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit eight times.
courses.prereqText: admittance to the MFA dance program or consent of instructor required.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Theatre Externship
courses.description: Selected professional opportunities in repertory and commercial theatre, designed to engage the student in particular creative responsibilities under the guidance of master artist-teachers. Student is expected to give biweekly reports detailing his/her experience with the professional company.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program, or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Acting Process III: Actors’ Studio
courses.description: An advanced studio for graduate actors and directors, this work will explore a single text from the modern theatre under the direction of a master teacher-artist. Concentration will be on multiple possible modes of encountering a text, varieties of interpretation and performance realization, and the development of a theatre ensemble.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Professional Preparation for the Actor
courses.description: A twice-weekly seminar focusing on the actor’s confrontation with the industry, including in-depth preparation for auditions; cold readings; and meetings/interviews with producers, casting directors, agents, and managers. Actors will also begin to create material that could be crafted into solo performances.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Acting for the Camera
courses.description: This course is designed to aid the actor in the transition from stage to film work. Examination of film production and its physical characteristics and the acting style needed for work in film and television. Students will rehearse and perform in simulated studio setting.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Singing for the Actor III
courses.description: Continuing vocal technique for the musical theatre. More complicated musical material investigated and prepared.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Skills
courses.description: A unifying approach to acting skills (voice, movement, and speech) designed to result in providing the graduating actor with a daily regimen appropriate for professional work.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Directing Seminar
courses.description: A seminar focusing on the current directing projects of all graduate directing students. Depending upon individual student needs, the work may include play selection, historical or sociological research, and discussion of emerging directorial concepts, the rehearsal process, and postproduction evaluation.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Director/Playwright/Choreographer Lab
courses.description: Collaborative process between directing and playwriting students providing a focused exploration of a broad range of directing and writing methodologies. Students work in teams to develop and create pieces based on the methodology of guest directors.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: New Plays Workshop
courses.description: A course where playwrights and actors work together to develop new plays-in-progress.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Directing Practicum
courses.description: Students enrolled in this course will work on productions in the function of a director. This will include staging, creative interpretation, blocking, etc.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Playwriting Seminar
courses.description: A seminar focusing on the current playwriting project of all graduate playwriting students. Work for each quarter is individually determined according to student needs, but may include exploration of an inceptive idea, development of a scenario or other structural work, and writing dialogue. Students present work to be discussed in class. May include group or individual playwriting exercises.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Playwriting Practicum
courses.description: Creative writing project developing original scripts from outline to the final play. Plays may vary depending on the quarter but will include writing of a realistic one-act, a nonrealistic one-act, a one-act documentary or dramatization of fiction, a full-length play.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Dramaturgy Seminar
courses.description: The seminar will deal with all dramaturgical issues pertaining to departmental productions: production research, textual and analysis, translation, adaptation, rehearsal process, and critique. Concurrently with the dramaturgy issues of the given year, the seminar will discuss possible choices of plays for future production seasons.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Dramaturgy Practicum
courses.description: Students enrolled in this course will work on productions in the function of a dramaturg. This will entail preparation of texts, research, participation at rehearsals, etc.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Television Writing
courses.description: A one-quarter course covering the hour-long format (five weeks) and situation comedies (five weeks). Includes study and discussion of television script format and structure. Students will create the concept and structure for spec scripts in each genre.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Writing for Performance
courses.description: This course is open to any graduate student who wants to expand their knowledge and experience of writing for performance. Open to graduate students who wish to incorporate writing into their creative and research practice. S/U grades only. May be taken for credit two times.
courses.prereqText: graduate standing and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Contemporary Plays
courses.description: A guided reading course focusing exclusively on very recent plays in an attempt to become aware of what is being written now. Course may be repeated for credit.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Screenwriting
courses.description: Students will develop the concept for an original piece for television or film and will write the screenplay. Student work will be discussed in seminar at each phase of the development.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program and THGR or TDGR 250.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Screenwriting
courses.description: Students will develop the concept for an original piece for television or film and will write the screenplay. Student work will be discussed in seminar at each phase of the development.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program and THGR or TDGR 250.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Dramatization and Adaptation
courses.description: Seminar will deal with dramatization and adaptation of literary texts for the purpose of theatrical production. The class will study some significant examples of such practice from the past and, subsequently, students will develop their own projects of dramatization, adaptation, or modernization of texts.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: New-Play Festival
courses.description: The collaborative process of new-play development through readings, rehearsals, and public performance. MFA actors, designers, directors, playwrights, and stage managers enroll in one section and collaborate in creating the annual festival of full-length and one-act plays.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Crossing Boundaries: Design Improvisations
courses.description: Conceiving interactive designs. A project/performance-based course, concentrating on the conception of designs adaptable to improvisatory contexts, in which technological strategies such as real-time processing and control of sound and light are encouraged and discussed.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Storyboarding
courses.description: Course will cover multiple applications of storyboarding as a tool of communication and expression; comic books, theatre, opera, film, TV, and commercial applications will be explored. Individual and team assignments will be given to develop the basic vocabulary and techniques.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Photoshop I
courses.description: Course will introduce the basic functions and applications of Photoshop as they may be applied to theatrical design. Emphasis on using Photoshop as an artistic tool.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Photoshop II
courses.description: Advanced Photoshop techniques will be explored and applied to the creation of multimedia projects.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Design Studio I
courses.description: This course will focus on beginning-level problems in theatre design, including text analysis, research, conceptualization, and visual expression. Students will work on individual projects in lighting, costume, and scenic design. The course will include group critiques of completed designs and works in progress. 270A, Scenic Design (fall); 270B, Costume Design (winter); 270C, Lighting Design (spring).
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Design Studio I: Costume Design
courses.description: This course will focus on beginning-level problems in theatre design, including text analysis, research, conceptualization, and visual expression. Students will work on individual projects in lighting, costume, and scenic design. The course will include group critiques of completed design and works in progress. 270A, Scenic Design (fall); 270B, Costume Design (winter); 270C, Lighting Design (spring).
courses.prereqText: THGR 270A, graduate standing, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Design Studio I: Lighting Design
courses.description: This course will focus on beginning-level problems in theatre design, including text analysis, research, conceptualization, and visual expression. Students will work on individual projects in lighting, costume, and scenic design. The course will include group critiques of completed design and works in progress. 270A, Scenic Design (fall); 270B, Costume Design (winter); 270C, Lighting Design (spring).
courses.prereqText: THGR 270A or TDGR 270A, THGR 270B or TDGR 270B, graduate standing, and consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Design Studio I: Sound Design
courses.description: This course will focus on beginning-level problems in theatre design, including text analysis, research, conceptualization, and visual/auditory expression. Students will work on individual projects in sound, lighting, costume, and scenic design. This course will include group critiques of completed design and works in progress. 270A, Scenic Design (fall); 270B, Costume Design (winter); 270C, Lighting Design (spring).
courses.prereqText: THGR 270A, THGR 270B, graduate standing, consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Design Seminar
courses.description: A seminar focusing on all aspects of the design profession, including current projects of graduate design students. The work may also include portfolio presentations, research presentations, and guest lecturers.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Fashioning the Body
courses.description: A survey/history of artistic and cultural stylistic change as embodied in clothing from early Western civilization to the contemporary period.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Advanced Scenic Design
courses.description: This course explores advanced problems in scenic design through development and critique of creative class projects and production works-in-progress.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Advanced Lighting Design
courses.description: Creative projects and topics in lighting design to develop the student’s techniques and professional practices. Work to include studies in design research, concepts, psychophysical considerations, collaboration, professional procedures and systems, paperwork, and organization. Various scales of production projects will be addressed by the student for presentation and critique and may be theoretical or productions in the departmental calendar.
courses.prereqText: second- or third-year design students only; admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Advanced Costume Design
courses.description: Projects in costume design, emphasizing script analysis, research, conceptualization, and visual expression. Studio work includes costume rendering in various media for specific plays.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Special Topics in Theatre Design
courses.description: A course designed to expose the theatre design student to a variety of specialized topics, including millinery, pattern drafting and draping, scenic painting, model making, figure drawing, drafting, fitting, rendering. Topics will vary from quarter to quarter.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Design Practicum
courses.description: This course covers the artistic, aesthetic, and practical aspects of the designers’ work as they develop and execute the design toward a fully realized production.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Stage Management 1
courses.description: Discussion and research into the duties, responsibilities, and roles of a stage manager. Work to include studies in script analysis, communication, conflict resolution, rehearsal procedures, performance skills, style, and conceptual approach to stage management.
courses.prereqText: admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Stage Management 2
courses.description: The second of the three-part introductory stage management series, this course further explores the stage manager’s process, focusing on the technical rehearsal period through the opening of a production.
courses.prereqText: TDGR 280A; admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Stage Management 3
courses.description: The final course in the three-part introductory stage management series focuses on the stage manager’s role once a production has opened. The course will also address topics such as new plays, touring, dance, multimedia productions, and music.
courses.prereqText: TDGR 280A and TDGR 280B; admission to MFA theatre program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Advanced Sound Design
courses.description: Creative projects to develop student’s techniques and professional practices. Studies include research, concepts, collaboration, professional procedures, systems and organization. Various scales of projects will be addressed for presentation and critique; may be theoretical or productions in the Department calendar.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA program or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Special Topics in Stage Management
courses.description: A course for MFA students in stage management. Topics will focus on various aspects of theatre administration, and advanced stage management, including nonprofit theatre, commercial theatre, advanced problems, venues, musicals/dance, production management, theatre development, business problems, and theatre marketing.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Stage Management Seminar
courses.description: A weekly seminar in which all graduate stage managers participate. Includes discussions of problems encountered on current productions, paperwork, methodology, and production approaches.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Introduction to Doctoral Studies
courses.description: Seminar acquaints doctoral students of all levels with research methods, theoretical models, publishing protocol, professional preparation, and pedagogical approaches particular to theatre and performance studies. Course assignments are tailored to students’ scholarly interests and progress toward degree.
courses.prereqText: admission to PhD program in theatre or consent of instructor.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Prospectus Class
courses.description: This course will support students in developing the dissertation prospectus. Through the course of the quarter and aided by readings (both theoretical and methodological), students will formulate their research problems as they relate to the fields of theatre, dance, and performance studies. Students will also clarify the primary objects, methods, and contributions of the dissertation. Participants will workshop their ideas and receive regular feedback.
courses.prereqText: admission to PhD program in theatre.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Dramatic Literature and Theatre History Prior to 1900
courses.description: Selected material from following topics: Classical Drama, Asian Drama, Medieval and Early Modern Drama, Shakespeare, European Drama 1600–1900. May be taken eight times as content varies.
courses.prereqText: admission to PhD program in theatre.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Dramatic Literature and Theatre History 1900 to the Present
courses.description: Selected material from following topics: European Theatre 1900–Present, American Theatre 1900–Present, Contemporary Theatre and Performance. May be taken eight times as content varies.
courses.prereqText: admission to PhD program in theatre.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Cultural and Critical Theory
courses.description: Selected material from following topics: Performance Theory, Dramatic Theory, Critical Theory, Cultural Studies. May be taken eight times as content varies.
courses.prereqText: admission to PhD program in theatre.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Directed Studies
courses.description: Individual or small group directed study.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Dissertation Research
courses.description: Research and preparation of doctoral dissertation.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Acting Practicum
courses.description: This course covers the artistic, aesthetic, and practical aspects of the actors’ work as they develop and execute the character/role toward a fully realized production.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Stage Management Practicum
courses.description: Taken each term by all graduate stage management students. The class focuses on the development of knowledge and skills necessary for the contemporary stage manager. Seminar format is augmented by lab work that may include departmental productions.
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Thesis Research
courses.description: Thesis research for MFA. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Thesis Project
courses.description: Specific projects in theatre individually determined to meet the developing needs, interests, and abilities of MFA candidates. (S/U grades only.)
courses.prereqText: admission to the MFA theatre program.

courses.subject: TDGR
courses.title: Introduction to Apprentice Teaching
courses.description: This course, designed to meet the needs of the graduate students who serve as teaching assistants, includes analysis of texts and materials, discussion of teaching techniques, conducting discussion sections, formulation of topics and questions for papers, and examinations and grading. Two units = twenty-five percent TAship. Four units = fifty percent TAship.
courses.prereqText: graduate standing and consent of the instructor.
